metadata.description: Representative dataset of Moroccan actors (economic-policy institutions, research bodies, leading firms, and training entities).
metadata.introduction: A granular representation of the evolution of key actors within the social region of Morocco. This dataset traces the formation, transformation, and significant milestones of policy, research, corporate, and training entities, from the Alaouite Makhzen and protectorate administrations through independence ministries and the central bank to industrial-acceleration agencies, public research bodies, universities, and export-oriented firms.

actors.description: The central bank of the Kingdom; issues the dirham, conducts monetary policy, and supervises banks through the CCSRS financial-stability committee.

events.description: Created by Dahir as the Banque du Maroc, issuing institute succeeding the Banque d'État du Maroc
New statute grants autonomy: price stability as primary mandate, Bank Al-Maghrib name adopted
Dirham fluctuation band widened, first step toward a flexible exchange-rate regime

actors.name: Bank Al-Maghrib

actors.description: Ministerial department setting economic, fiscal, and financial policy; steers the budget, customs, taxes, treasury, and state shareholdings.

events.description: Finance portfolio created in the first post-independence government
Structural-adjustment program launches liberalization and fiscal consolidation
Organic finance law (LOLF) modernizes budget programming and performance

actors.name: Ministry of Economy and Finance

actors.description: Directorate inside the MEF producing the macro framework, forecasts, and competitiveness studies behind each finance law.

events.description: Economic-studies and forecasting function organized within the ministry
Formalized as the Directorate of Studies and Financial Forecasts (DEPF)

actors.name: Directorate of Studies and Financial Forecasts (DEPF)

actors.description: Ministry driving industrial acceleration plans, trade policy, and the automotive, aeronautics, and offshoring ecosystems.

events.description: Industry and commerce portfolio established at independence
Industrial Acceleration Plan (2014-2020) launches sectoral ecosystems
New industrial strategy targets investment charter and import substitution

actors.name: Ministry of Industry and Trade

actors.description: Public agency promoting private investment and export development under the investment charter.

events.description: Created by merging investment and export promotion bodies
New investment charter assigns AMDIE a central one-stop-shop role

actors.name: Moroccan Agency for Investment and Export Development (AMDIE)

actors.description: Independent authority regulating the Casablanca capital market and investor protection.

events.description: CDVM securities regulator created alongside market modernization
Re-founded as the AMMC with extended powers over market infrastructure

actors.name: Moroccan Capital Market Authority (AMMC)

actors.description: Authority supervising insurance, reinsurance, brokerage, and social-welfare bodies.

events.description: Insurance supervision department (DAPS) modernized
ACAPS established as independent supervisory authority

actors.name: Supervisory Authority of Insurance and Social Welfare (ACAPS)

actors.description: Administration enforcing foreign-exchange regulations and tracking external financial flows.

events.description: Exchange-control administration organized after currency sovereignty
Gradual convertibility measures ease current-account operations

actors.name: Office des Changes

actors.description: Africa's third stock exchange by capitalization; lists banking, telecom, mining, and industrial groups.

events.description: Stock exchange founded in Casablanca
Demutualized and computerized under market reforms
Adopts NSC trading platform shared with Euronext markets

actors.name: Casablanca Stock Exchange

actors.description: Customs and indirect-tax administration collecting duties and policing trade at ports including Tanger Med.

events.description: Customs administration nationalized at independence
New customs code aligns procedures with international trade
Paperless BADR clearance system generalized across ports

actors.name: Administration of Customs and Indirect Taxes

actors.description: Constitutional consultative body advising on economic, social, and environmental policy and inclusive development.

events.description: Created by the 2011 constitution
New Development Model report frames post-Covid policy consensus

actors.name: Economic, Social and Environmental Council (CESE)

actors.description: Non-profit private research university backed by OCP; anchor of Morocco's applied-research and AI ecosystem with the Toubkal supercomputer.

events.description: Founded by the OCP Foundation in Benguerir
Green Tech Institute, School of Computer Science, and African Supercomputing Center launched
Co-operator of the national research, development, and innovation program (PNARDI) with CNRST

actors.name: Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P)

actors.description: National center funding, coordinating, and evaluating public scientific research and doctoral training.

events.description: Created to coordinate national scientific and technical research
IMIST information institute and associated research units attached
Co-operator of the national research, development, and innovation program (PNARDI) with UM6P

actors.name: National Center for Scientific and Technical Research (CNRST)

actors.description: Public institute for solar energy and new-energy research, testing, and pilot platforms.

events.description: Founded to support the Moroccan Solar Plan (Noor)
Noor Ouarzazate complex phases come online, anchoring test programs

actors.name: Research Institute for Solar Energy and New Energies (IRESEN)

actors.description: National agronomic research institute serving rainfed and irrigated agriculture, cereals, and arid-zone farming.

events.description: Reorganized as the national agronomic research institute
Regional centers aligned with the Green Morocco Plan

actors.name: National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA)

actors.description: Foundation for advanced materials, microelectronics, and biotechnology transfer to industry.

events.description: Founded as a public-utility research foundation
Microelectronics and biotech platforms opened to industrial partners

actors.name: Moroccan Foundation for Advanced Science, Innovation and Research (MAScIR)

actors.description: Corporate R&D and venturing arm of the phosphate group, industrializing green ammonia, batteries, and agtech pilots.

events.description: Launched as OCP's innovation and venturing vehicle
Startup campus and deeptech fund deployed around Benguerir

actors.name: InnovX (OCP innovation arm)

actors.description: Biomedical research and public-health laboratory network; historic center for vaccines, serums, and epidemics surveillance.

events.description: Institut Pasteur established in Casablanca
Covid-19 testing and genomic-surveillance backbone

actors.name: Institut Pasteur du Maroc

actors.description: Highest scientific authority advising on research policy, academy sessions, and national scientific prizes.

events.description: Created by Dahir as the national academy of sciences
Rabat headquarters inaugurated; resident members installed

actors.name: Hassan II Academy of Sciences and Techniques

actors.description: State phosphate and fertilizer group; world's largest phosphate exporter and engine of the Benguerir research ecosystem.

events.description: Office Chérifien des Phosphates created; Khouribga mining begins
Converted into a public limited company (OCP S.A.)
Jorf Lasfar fertilizer hub and slurry pipeline commissioned; African expansion accelerates

actors.name: OCP Group

actors.description: Automaker operating the Tanger Med plant, the largest car factory in Africa, driving the export-oriented ecosystem.

events.description: SOMACA assembly plant founded in Casablanca
Renault Tanger Med plant inaugurated with 340,000-unit capacity
Dacia Jogger and Mobilize Duo assigned, deepening local integration

actors.name: Renault Maroc

actors.description: Automaker operating the Kénitra plant and supplier park; second pillar of the Moroccan car ecosystem.

events.description: PSA Kénitra plant inaugurated
Capacity doubled toward 200,000 units with Citroën Ami and Opel Rocks-e

actors.name: Stellantis Kénitra

actors.description: Public utility for electricity generation planning and drinking-water supply; operator of Noor solar and grid extension.

events.description: Office National de l'Électricité created for rural electrification
ONE and ONEP merged into ONEE (electricity and water)
Near-universal electrification achieved; Noor Midelt program launched

actors.name: National Office of Electricity and Drinking Water (ONEE)

actors.description: Historic telecom operator and largest listed group alongside banks; pan-African carrier across ten countries.

events.description: Split from the postal-telecom office as Maroc Telecom
Listed in Casablanca and Paris; Vivendi takes control
Etisalat acquires Vivendi's stake; Moov Africa footprint built

actors.name: Maroc Telecom

actors.description: Largest banking group in Morocco and North Africa by market value; pan-African network across 25 countries.

events.description: BCM-Wafabank merger creates Attijariwafa bank
Sub-Saharan expansion via CBAO, BIM, and Société Générale buyouts
Top-ranked North African listed company by market capitalization

actors.name: Attijariwafa Bank

actors.description: Mutual-cooperative banking group rooted in popular banks; second-largest lender and major African footprint.

events.description: Banques Populaires network organized by Dahir
Listed vehicle BCP consolidates the group
Atlantic Bank and Banque Atlantique anchor West African growth

actors.name: Banque Centrale Populaire (BCP)

actors.description: Universal bank with historic trade-finance franchise and growing East and West African network.

events.description: Banque Marocaine du Commerce Extérieur founded for foreign trade
Rebranded Bank of Africa with continental ambitions
Casablanca Finance City headquarters tower completed

actors.name: Bank of Africa (BMCE Group)

actors.description: Mining and metallurgy group active in gold, cobalt, and copper across Morocco and sub-Saharan Africa.

events.description: Mining origins in the Anti-Atlas precious-metals belt
Reorganized as Managem, the mining arm of Al Mada
Cobalt and copper projects positioned for battery value chains

actors.name: Managem

actors.description: Port operator managing Casablanca and Nador terminals; key beneficiary of Tanger Med transshipment growth.

events.description: Split from the ports office (ODEP) as Marsa Maroc
Listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange
Nador West Med concession extends the terminal portfolio

actors.name: Marsa Maroc

actors.description: Largest private electricity producer operating the Jorf Lasfar coal complex; backbone of baseload supply.

events.description: Jorf Lasfar independent power project awarded
Abu Dhabi TAQA takes control
Listed among the top North African companies by market value

actors.name: TAQA Morocco

actors.description: Flag carrier connecting Casablanca's hub to Europe, Africa, and the Americas; Oneworld member.

events.description: Royal Air Maroc formed from Air Atlas and Air Maroc
Casablanca hub strategy targets West African connections
Joins the Oneworld alliance

actors.name: Royal Air Maroc

actors.description: Sugar refining group controlling the national quota; agro-industrial pillar from Doukkala to Gharb.

events.description: Sugar refineries established in Casablanca
Privatized to the SNI/ONA holding
Listed subsidiary mills consolidated under Cosumar group

actors.name: Cosumar

actors.description: Fuel distribution and retail leader; downstream anchor of the Akwa Group conglomerate.

events.description: Afriquia fuel distribution network founded
Storage and LPG positions built nationwide
Among the top Moroccan groups by revenue alongside OCP and Renault

actors.name: Afriquia SMDC

actors.description: Oldest university and largest doctoral-training system; core of public research output.

events.description: Mohammed V University founded in Rabat
Split into Agdal and Souissi universities, reunified in 2021
Top-ranked Moroccan university in global rankings

actors.name: Mohammed V University of Rabat

actors.description: Metropolitan university of Greater Casablanca; engineering, medicine, and management training hub.

events.description: University of Hassan II founded in Casablanca
Merged with Mohammedia university into a single institution

actors.name: Hassan II University of Casablanca

actors.description: Selective English-language public university modeled on the American system; business and engineering elite training.

events.description: Founded by royal Dahir in Ifrane
First cohort admitted; AACSB-accredited business school follows

actors.name: Al Akhawayn University

actors.description: Premier grande-école training state engineers for ministries, utilities, and industry since independence.

events.description: École Mohammadia d'Ingénieurs founded in Rabat
Computing and telecoms tracks feed the offshoring boom

actors.name: École Mohammadia d'Ingénieurs (EMI)

actors.description: National school of computer science and systems analysis; backbone of the digital-services talent pipeline.

events.description: ENSIAS founded in Rabat
Data, AI, and cybersecurity tracks scaled with offshoring demand

actors.name: National School of Computer Science (ENSIAS)

actors.description: Public vocational-training office running institutes (ISTA/ITA) across regions; mass technician and crafts training.

events.description: OFPPT created for vocational training
Sectoral institutes aligned with industrial ecosystems (auto, aero, textile)

actors.name: Office of Vocational Training (OFPPT)

actors.description: Tuition-free peer-learning coding schools backed by OCP/UM6P; gamified software-engineer pipeline.

events.description: 1337 Khouribga campus opened on the 42 model
Benguerir and YouCode satellites extend the network

actors.name: 1337 Coding School
